items.summary: Rescan with the fixed scan_nvidia: src/libs/cuda/helper_cuda.h and helper_string.h carry the pre-2017 CUDA samples EULA-pointer notice (the known cuda_voxelizer case that motivated the EULA markers). Standing was established by reading, but no recorded ruling exists; needs a person's confirmation. POLICY (2026-08-24): swap helper_cuda.h/helper_string.h for NVIDIA's BSD-3-Clause 2022 versions at the tip BEFORE any fork is created; never host the proprietary vintage at our tip.

Before the upstream PR: run the CUDA build (USE_HIP OFF, CUDAARCHS matching the GPU) on a real NVIDIA GPU at head and confirm -s 64 takes the GPU path and matches -cpu, so the Test Plans of 94d1340 and 8b84b91 (which show ./build/cuda_voxelizer -f ./test_models/bunny.OBJ -s 64 as a GPU run) are true. nvcc 12.8 build+link is already done at 689b885, 94d1340, 8b84b91 with no GPU. If no NVIDIA run is possible, correct those two Test Plans at the PR-prep squash instead.

At the PR-prep squash, correct the 3625a1e ([ROCm] Keep the voxel table in device memory) commit body: (1) 'as in the CUDA build' for the 512 boundary residual is unobserved (CUDA has only been run at -s 64); reword, or run the 512 matrix on an NVIDIA GPU. (2) State the CUDA trade-off: a cudaMalloc voxel table larger than free device memory now fails where a managed table oversubscribed on Linux/Pascal+ (e.g. -s 4096 = 8 GiB table). Whether that trade-off is acceptable or the port should instead use HIP-guarded _system atomics with a managed table is a person's call.

README Linux ROCm build line sets no CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE, so clang compiles HIP device code at -O0 (gfx1201: code objects equal the -O0 Debug build; GPU path 50-60x slower than Release, 512 surface 1635 ms vs 25.6 ms). Results are correct. Fix: add -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release to the Linux line as the Windows line already has (docs-only commit, carried forward). Porter at PR prep or now; a person rules.

decided.note: relayed in the linux-gfx1100 porter dispatch 2026-11-04
